items.title: Microsoft Entra ID Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Exploited in Wild, Allows Remote Code Execution
items.description: Microsoft on Thursday warned of a maximum-severity security flaw in Entra ID that it said has been exploited in the wild, but noted that no customer action is required. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-69836 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of remote code execution impacting the tech giant's cloud-based identity and access management service. It was previously called Azure Active Directory
items.action_detail: Confirmed exploitation or trivially weaponisable — act within 24h
items.ai_summary: CVE-2026-69836 is a maximum-severity remote code execution vulnerability affecting Microsoft Entra ID due to the deserialization of untrusted data. Although exploited in the wild, Microsoft has stated that no direct customer action is required because the flaw resides in the cloud service. The issue enables unauthorized remote actors to execute code over the network. Mitigation is handled entirely by Microsoft on the cloud-based identity and access management infrastructure.
items.why_it_matters: Cloud administrators can monitor advisory updates while Microsoft handles mitigation on the cloud-managed Entra ID service.
